## Executive Summary

**What changed**: A new internal web application, Locator Lens, has been built from scratch. The application accepts either a public URL or raw HTML, analyzes the page, discovers 8 categories of UI elements, generates XPath locators for each element using a priority-ordered strategy, and extracts computed style metadata — all delivered as a self-contained HTML report rendered directly in the user's browser.

**Why it matters**: QA engineers previously spent significant time manually inspecting pages to identify automation locators and document element properties. Locator Lens eliminates that manual step; engineers receive a production-ready locator report within the 30-second target for typical pages.

**Merge recommendation**: READY FOR MERGE. All 8 SDLC phases completed and approved. 104/104 tests pass (95% coverage), flake8 clean, live end-to-end verification confirmed by the quality-release-engineer. Three non-blocking minor observations are documented for optional post-release follow-up.

---

## Business Context

**Problem addressed**: Manual web-page inspection to identify automation-friendly locators is time-consuming, error-prone, and inconsistent across engineers. Locator quality varies and documentation of element metadata (fonts, colors, attributes) is rarely captured during the automation-scripting phase.

**Business goals**:
- Reduce time-to-locator for QA automation development.
- Standardize locator quality by applying a rules-based priority strategy (ID > unique attribute > relative XPath).
- Surface element metadata (computed font family, size, color, visible text) in a single browser session without additional tooling.

**User impact**: QA Engineers, UI Automation Engineers, and Test Engineers on the internal team can analyze any web page — live URL or pasted/uploaded HTML — in under 30 seconds and receive a structured HTML report with all locator and style information needed for automation script development.

## Technical Summary

### Architecture

Single-process, stateless FastAPI application (Uvicorn ASGI server) with an 8-module pipeline:

1. **Web UI / Entry Form** — Jinja2 server-rendered form; HTML POST to `/analyze`.
2. **FastAPI Application Layer** — routing, Pydantic request validation, single-analysis `threading.Lock`, exception-to-HTTP mapping.
3. **Input Acquisition** — URL validation (http/https only), Playwright/Chromium navigation with 30s timeout and 5-redirect cap, `page.route()` size-cap interception (~5MB), and raw-HTML/upload UTF-8 decode with pre-decode size check.
4. **DOM Parsing & Element Discovery** — BeautifulSoup/lxml tolerant parsing; `data-ll-idx` marker injection for BS4-to-Playwright element correlation; 8-type element classification; hidden/iframe/viewport exclusion rules.
5. **XPath Generation** — priority-ordered rule-based strategy with `lxml.etree.XPath()` syntax validation and fragility tagging.
6. **Style Metadata Extraction** — `getComputedStyle` via live Playwright handle (rendered mode); `tinycss2` simple-selector cascade approximation (raw-HTML mode); shared hex color normalization utility.
7. **Report Assembly** — Jinja2-rendered HTML report with app-name/tech-stack auto-detection, 8-column element table, consistent "Not Available" styling, and autoescaping for XSS safety.
8. **Cross-Cutting Error/Logging** — typed exception hierarchy (`InvalidUrlError`, `FetchTimeoutError`, `TlsValidationError`, `UnparseableContentError`, `NoElementsFoundError`, `PageTooLargeError`), console + rotating-file logger.

### Significant Technical Decisions

- **FastAPI over Flask**: native async route support aligns with Playwright's async-first API; free OpenAPI/Swagger documentation at `/docs`.
- **`data-ll-idx` marker injection** (design-review Must-Do #1): a single `page.evaluate()` call assigns sequential integer markers to all 8-type elements in DOM order immediately after render, then `page.content()` is captured so the BeautifulSoup tree and the live Playwright DOM share the same identifiers. O(1) handle resolution thereafter via `page.locator(f'[data-ll-idx="{node_key}"]')`.
- **`page.route()` size-cap interception** (design-review Must-Do #2): document-resource requests are intercepted before the body is delivered to the Playwright page; a `Content-Length` fast path and a `response.body()` slow path both enforce the ~5MB ceiling and abort before any oversized body enters the renderer.
- **Sync route handlers**: plain `def` routes run in Starlette's thread-pool, simplifying the single-lock/single-analysis-at-a-time model without needing async bridging.
- **Redirect count verified at runtime**: rather than treating the Playwright redirect-count question as a spike, `input_acquisition._count_redirects` walks `request.redirected_from` post-navigation and raises `TooManyRedirectsError` above 5 hops.

## Quality Summary

### Code Review Outcome

**Status: APPROVED** (`documents/code-review.md`, Phase 6, 2026-09-01).

Both design-review Must-Do conditions verified correct by the code-reviewer (independent re-read + test run). No CRITICAL or MAJOR correctness, security, or standards issues found. Three MINOR observations (non-blocking; carried forward as optional follow-up items):

- MINOR-1: `tech_detect.py` at 86% coverage — script-src framework-detection heuristic branches untested; safe "Not Available" fallback already in place.
- MINOR-2: TLS failures in URL-mode briefly classified as `RenderError` before resolving to `TlsValidationError` via fallback — cosmetically produces an unnecessary "degraded" notice; end-user outcome is still correct.
- MINOR-3: `logging_config.py` file-handler-failure defensive branches untested — acceptable for a local/dev-only tool.

### Test Results

| Metric | Result | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Tests passed | 104 / 104 | All pass |
| Overall coverage | 95% | ≥80% |
| Critical-path modules (validation, parsing, discovery, XPath, style) | 92–100% | ≥80% |
| Unit tests | 78 | — |
| Integration tests | 26 | — |
| Live E2E verification (QA session) | Passed | — |
| Flake8 (PEP 8) findings | 0 | 0 |
| Flakiness observed across 3 independent runs | None | None |

Test suite uses fixture HTML files and a local `http.server` + real Playwright/Chromium instance — no live public websites, per the testing policy in `documents/requirements.md`.

### Security Validation

- **XSS**: Jinja2 `select_autoescape(["html"])` active; no `| safe` filter anywhere in templates. All analyzed-page content flows through `{{ }}` and is HTML-escaped by default. Confirmed by code-reviewer grep and XSS-escaping assertion in `tests/unit/test_report.py`.
- **TLS**: Never disabled. Playwright's default certificate validation enforced; `httpx` fallback client uses `verify=True` explicitly.
- **URL scheme**: Restricted to `http`/`https` before any network call. `file://`, `javascript:`, and other schemes rejected.
- **Size bounding**: ~5MB enforced on both input paths.
- **Stack-trace leakage**: none — unexpected exceptions logged server-side only; generic safe message returned to client.
- **File upload handling**: content read into memory only; client-supplied filename is used only as a display label, never to construct a filesystem path.
- **SSRF**: Deliberate accepted risk (no RFC1918/loopback blocking) — consistent with the requirements' explicit "no cross-domain restrictions; no allowlist/blocklist" decision for this internal trusted-network tool. Documented in `documents/design-document.md` Threat Analysis.

### Performance Validation

No performance regressions. Architecture's stated envelope (30s fetch/render bound, ~5MB input cap, single-threaded single-analysis-at-a-time) is unchanged since design approval. Test suite runs consistently in under 30 seconds (observed: 9–27s across three QA passes).

## Known Risks & Limitations

| Item | Type | Status | Mitigation / Follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw-HTML CSS cascade approximation is intentionally narrow (simple selectors only) | Accepted architectural limitation | Carry forward | Returns "Not Available" rather than guessing; documented in developer guide and report degradation notice |
| SSRF — no RFC1918/loopback blocking | Accepted risk (requirements-driven) | Carry forward | Redirect cap (5) and 30s timeout bound blast radius; intended for trusted internal team only |
| Single in-process lock: one hung analysis blocks until 30s timeout fires | Known limitation | Carry forward | Hard 30s timeout + `finally`-block lock release already in place |
| MINOR-1: `tech_detect.py` script-src branches untested (86%) | Minor quality gap | Optional follow-up | Safe "Not Available" fallback; non-critical path |
| MINOR-2: TLS errors briefly classified as `RenderError` (cosmetic mislabel only) | Minor UX gap | Optional follow-up | Suggested fix: inspect exception message in `_make_route_handler` for TLS indicators |
| MINOR-3: `logging_config.py` file-handler-failure path untested | Minor coverage gap | Optional follow-up | Defensive code for unlikely filesystem-permission scenario |
| Playwright/Chromium binary dependency adds first-run setup step | Environment setup | Carry forward | Documented in README and Makefile (`make setup`); `playwright install chromium` |

No risk above is rated Critical or High-impact at the MVP scope.

## Release Notes

### Locator Lens — Initial Release (MVP)

**What's new**: Locator Lens is a new internal web application for QA and UI Automation engineers. Submit any public web page URL or raw/pasted HTML and receive a structured HTML report in your browser containing:

- Auto-detected Application Name and Frontend Technology stack.
- A table of all discovered interactive and structural elements (headings, links, buttons, inputs, dropdowns, textareas, and clickable role-based elements), with:
  - The best available XPath locator using a priority-ordered strategy (ID-based → unique attribute → shortest robust relative XPath). Locators identified as potentially fragile are marked "** Fragile **".
  - Computed font family, font size, and font color for elements with visible text (or "Not Available" when unresolvable).
  - All relevant HTML attributes (id, name, class, data-*, aria-*).
- Clear, actionable error messages for invalid URLs, network failures, TLS issues, and unparseable content.
- Partial failure indicators: elements that fail individual processing steps are marked "Failed"/"Skipped" with a reason, rather than aborting the entire analysis.

**Not included in this release**: login-protected pages, multi-page crawling, iframe content analysis, screenshots, accessibility audits, concurrent analyses, mobile UI, or persistence of results. These are explicitly out of scope for the MVP.

## Deployment Guidance

This is a **local/dev-only** deployment — no staging or production tier, no containerization required.

```bash
# 1. Clone/check out the release commit
git checkout <release-commit-or-tag>

# 2. Create and activate a Python virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/activate        # Windows
# source .venv/bin/activate   # macOS/Linux

# 3. Install Python dependencies and the Chromium browser
pip install -r requirements.txt
playwright install chromium

# 4. Run the test suite (optional but recommended)
pytest --cov=src/app --cov-report=term-missing -q

# 5. Start the application
cd src
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
# (add --reload for active development)

# 6. Verify
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health   # expect {"status":"ok"}
```

Equivalent `make` targets are available: `make setup`, `make test`, `make lint`, `make run`.

**No environment variables, secrets, or external service configuration are required.** The application has no authentication, no database, and no external API dependencies.

**Post-deployment smoke check**: open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` in a browser, submit a test URL or the raw-HTML sample below, and confirm a report renders:

```html
<html><head><title>Test Page</title></head><body>
<h1 id="main-title">Welcome</h1>
<a href="/login" id="login-link">Login</a>
<button data-testid="submit-btn">Submit</button>
</body></html>
```

Expected result: "Total Elements: 3", ID-based XPaths for the `h1` and `a`, data-testid-based XPath for the `button`.

---

## Rollback Guidance

Since the application is **stateless with no database** (no persistent data to reconcile), rollback is equivalent to redeploying the previous commit:

```bash
# 1. Stop the running process (Ctrl+C or terminate by PID/port)

# 2. Check out the previous known-good commit
git checkout <previous-release-commit-or-tag>

# 3. Re-sync dependencies (only if requirements.txt changed)
pip install -r requirements.txt
playwright install chromium   # only if Chromium version pin changed

# 4. Restart
cd src
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

# 5. Verify
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

No data migration, no database state, and no persisted analysis history to reconcile.

## Monitoring Considerations

- **`GET /health`** endpoint returns `{"status":"ok"}` and serves as the primary liveness check. Verify this after startup and after any restart.
- **Log file**: `logs/locator-lens.log` (rotating file handler) captures request lifecycle, timing, and exception detail server-side. Console output is also available in the uvicorn terminal.
- **Post-release validation focus**: confirm that both URL-mode and raw-HTML-mode analyses produce reports for typical internal pages (confirm XPath locators appear; confirm "Not Available" for styles where no CSS is present).
- **Single-analysis lock**: if the app appears unresponsive, check whether a prior analysis is still running (it will unblock within the 30s timeout). Monitor the log for timeout/lock-release events.
